items.title: Types of Forces
items.body: Weight \(W=mg\), Normal reaction \(N\), Tension \(T\), Friction \(F\leq\mu N\). Forces are vectors — resolve horizontally and vertically.

items.title: Equilibrium
items.body: A particle is in equilibrium when the resultant force is zero: \(\sum F_x=0\) and \(\sum F_y=0\). Use triangle/polygon of forces.

items.title: Resolving Forces
items.body: Force \(F\) at angle \(\theta\): horizontal component \(F\cos\theta\), vertical component \(F\sin\theta\).

items.title: Friction
items.body: Limiting friction: \(F=\mu N\). When moving: \(F=\mu N\). Static: \(F\leq\mu N\). \(\mu\) is the coefficient of friction.

items.title: Lami's Theorem
items.body: For three concurrent forces in equilibrium: \(\dfrac{F_1}{\sin\alpha}=\dfrac{F_2}{\sin\beta}=\dfrac{F_3}{\sin\gamma}\)

items.title: Inclined Planes
items.body: On slope at angle \(\alpha\): component along slope \(=mg\sin\alpha\), perpendicular \(=mg\cos\alpha\).

body.en: A force is a vector (magnitude + direction). The resultant of forces is found by vector addition; for equilibrium the resultant is zero. Resolve forces into horizontal and vertical components: \(F_x=F\cos\theta\), \(F_y=F\sin\theta\). Friction force satisfies \(F\leq\mu R\); limiting equilibrium: \(F=\mu R\).

body.en: Proportional Invariance, Linear Structure & Quantitative Modeling: Across Cambridge International AS Level (9709 Paper 1 / Paper 4 / Paper 5), multi-step problems reduce to identifying invariant quantities—constant rates of change \(m = \dfrac{\Delta y}{\Delta x}\), conservation of total work/mass, or linear system rank conditions. A two-variable linear system \(a_1 x + b_1 y = c_1\), \(a_2 x + b_2 y = c_2\) has a unique intersection if \(\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} \ne \dfrac{b_1}{b_2}\), no solution (parallel lines) if \(\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} = \dfrac{b_1}{b_2} \ne \dfrac{c_1}{c_2}\), and infinitely many solutions if all three ratios coincide.

body.en:
Normal reaction is perpendicular to the plane: On an inclined plane of angle \(\alpha\), the normal reaction is \(R = mg\cos\alpha\) (if no other perpendicular forces act). Assuming \(R = mg\) on an inclined plane is an instant fatal error.

Gravity components on a slope: Gravity acts vertically downward. Its resolved components are \(mg\sin\alpha\) acting down the slope and \(mg\cos\alpha\) acting perpendicularly into the plane.

Friction is reactive: The friction force obeys \(F \le \mu R\). It only equals \(\mu R\) when motion is impending (limiting equilibrium) or actively occurring. If a system is stationary and not on the verge of slipping, \(F\) balances whatever force opposes it, satisfying \(F < \mu R\).

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Forces & Equilibrium)

body.en:
Why Successive Multipliers & Harmonic Average Speed Work: If a quantity \(Q_0\) undergoes a percentage change \(p\%\) followed by \(q\%\), the compound multiplier is the product of individual scale factors:

\[ Q_{\text{final}} = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p}{100}\right)\!\left(1 + \frac{q}{100}\right) = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p + q}{100} + \frac{pq}{10000}\right) \]

Notice the cross term \(\dfrac{pq}{10000}\): an increase of \(p\%\) followed by a decrease of \(p\%\) yields \(Q_0\bigl(1 - (p/100)^2\bigr) < Q_0\). Similarly, traveling equal distance \(d\) at speeds \(v_1\) and \(v_2\) takes total time \(T = \frac{d}{v_1} + \frac{d}{v_2}\), so average speed is the harmonic mean \(v_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{2d}{d/v_1 + d/v_2} = \dfrac{2v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2}\).

label.en: Worked example 2 — Friction on an inclined plane

problem.en: A block of mass 5 kg lies on a rough plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal (\(\mu=0.4\), \(g=10\) m/s²). Find the friction force acting when the block is on the point of sliding down.

solution.en:
Normal reaction: \(R=5g\cos30°=50\times\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\approx43.3\) N.

Friction (limiting, up the slope): \(F=0.4\times43.3\approx17.3\) N.

Check: Gravity component down slope \(=50\sin30°=25\) N \(\gt F\), so block would slide — friction acts up slope.

problem.en: A particle of mass \(m\) kg is placed on a rough inclined plane. The plane is inclined at an angle \(\alpha\) to the horizontal, where \(\tan \alpha = \frac{3}{4}\). The particle is on the point of sliding down the plane. The coefficient of static friction between the particle and the plane is \(\mu_s\). Given that the acceleration due to gravity is \(g = 9.8 \text{ m/s}^2\), find the value of \(\mu_s\).

solution.en: When a particle is on the point of sliding down an inclined plane, the angle of inclination \(\alpha\) is equal to the angle of friction \(\phi\), where \(\tan \phi = \mu_s\). \nGiven that \(\tan \alpha = \frac{3}{4}\), and the particle is on the point of sliding, we have \(\alpha = \phi\). \nTherefore, \(\mu_s = \tan \phi = \tan \alpha = \frac{3}{4}\).

label.en: Worked Example 4 — Equilibrium of Three Coplanar Forces
label.ar: مثال محلول 4 — اتزان ثلاث قوى مستوية

problem.en: Three horizontal forces of magnitudes \(8\text{ N}\), \(15\text{ N}\), and \(P\text{ N}\) keep a particle in equilibrium. If the \(8\text{ N}\) force acts due East and the \(15\text{ N}\) force acts due North, find the magnitude \(P\) and the bearing of the third force to the nearest degree.
problem.ar: تؤثر ثلاث قوى أفقية مقاديرها \(8\text{ N}\) و\(15\text{ N}\) و\(P\text{ N}\) في جسيم في حالة اتزان. إذا أثرت القوة \(8\text{ N}\) نحو الشرق والقوة \(15\text{ N}\) نحو الشمال، فأوجد المقدار \(P\) واتجاه القوة الثالثة مقرباً إلى أقرب درجة.

solution.en:
For equilibrium, the horizontal components sum to zero: \(P_x = -8\text{ N}\) (West) and \(P_y = -15\text{ N}\) (South).

Magnitude: \[P = \sqrt{8^2 + 15^2} = \sqrt{64 + 225} = \sqrt{289} = 17\text{ N}.\]

Acute angle South of West: \(\tan\alpha = \frac{15}{8} \implies \alpha \approx 61.9^\circ\), or West of South \(\tan\beta = \frac{8}{15} \implies \beta \approx 28.1^\circ\), so the bearing is \(180^\circ + 28^\circ = 208^\circ\).
solution.ar:
لتحقق الاتزان ينعدم مجموع المركّبات: \(P_x = -8\text{ N}\) (غرباً) و\(P_y = -15\text{ N}\) (جنوباً).

المقدار: \[P = \sqrt{8^2 + 15^2} = \sqrt{289} = 17\text{ N}.\]

الزاوية غرب الجنوب \(\beta = \arctan(\tfrac{8}{15}) \approx 28.1^\circ\)، فيكون الاتجاه الدائري الحقيقي \(180^\circ + 28^\circ = 208^\circ\).

body.en: High-Speed Exam Shortcut (Cambridge International AS Level (9709 Paper 1 / Paper 4 / Paper 5)): When a linear system asks for a combined expression like \(3x + 3y\) rather than \(x\) and \(y\) individually, add or subtract the two equations directly before isolating either variable—this often yields the target expression in a single step.

question.en: A block of mass \(8\text{ kg}\) rests in limiting equilibrium on a rough plane inclined at \(30^\circ\) to the horizontal. Taking \(g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2\): (a) calculate the normal reaction \(R\), (b) find the coefficient of friction \(\mu\) between the block and the plane.

solution.en: (a) Resolve perpendicular to the inclined plane: \[R = mg\cos 30^\circ = 8(9.8)\cos 30^\circ = 78.4 \times \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 39.2\sqrt{3} \approx 67.9\text{ N (3 s.f.)}\] (b) Resolve parallel to the plane. Since the block is in limiting equilibrium on the verge of sliding down, friction \(F = \mu R\) acts up the plane: \[F = mg\sin 30^\circ = 8(9.8)\sin 30^\circ = 78.4 \times 0.5 = 39.2\text{ N}\] Setting \(F = \mu R\): \[\mu = \dfrac{F}{R} = \dfrac{mg\sin 30^\circ}{mg\cos 30^\circ} = \tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{3} \approx 0.577\text{ (3 s.f.)}\]

hints.en: (a) Resolve perpendicular to the inclined plane: \(R = mg\cos 30^\circ = 8(9.8)\cos 30^\circ = 78.4 \times \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 39.2\sqrt{3}\).

(b) Resolve parallel to the plane. Since the block is in limiting equilibrium on the verge of sliding down, friction \(F = \mu R\) acts up the plane: \(F = mg\sin 30^\circ = 8(9.8)\sin 30^\circ = 78.4 \times 0.5\).

hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(F = \mu R\) ، \(\mu = \dfrac{F}{R} = \dfrac{mg\sin 30^\circ}{mg\cos 30^\circ} = \tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

question.en: A small particle of weight \(24\text{ N}\) is held in equilibrium by two light inextensible strings. String \(A\) makes an angle of \(30^\circ\) with the upward vertical, and string \(B\) makes an angle of \(60^\circ\) with the upward vertical. Find the tensions \(T_A\) and \(T_B\) in the two strings.

solution.en:
Notice that the angle between string \(A\) and string \(B\) is \(30^\circ + 60^\circ = 90^\circ\), so the strings are perpendicular.
Resolve horizontally: \[T_A\sin 30^\circ = T_B\sin 60^\circ \Rightarrow T_A(0.5) = T_B\left(\tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) \Rightarrow T_A = \sqrt{3}T_B\] Resolve vertically: \[T_A\cos 30^\circ + T_B\cos 60^\circ = 24 \Rightarrow T_A\left(\tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) + T_B(0.5) = 24\] Substitute \(T_A = \sqrt{3}T_B\): \[(\sqrt{3}T_B)\left(\tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) + 0.5T_B = 24 \Rightarrow \tfrac{3}{2}T_B + \tfrac{1}{2}T_B = 24 \Rightarrow 2T_B = 24 \Rightarrow T_B = 12\text{ N}\] Then: \[T_A = 12\sqrt{3} \approx 20.8\text{ N (3 s.f.)}\]

hints.en: Notice that the angle between string \(A\) and string \(B\) is \(30^\circ + 60^\circ = 90^\circ\), so the strings are perpendicular.
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(A\) ، \(B\) ، \(30^\circ + 60^\circ = 90^\circ\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

hints.en: Resolve horizontally: \(T_A\sin 30^\circ = T_B\sin 60^\circ \Rightarrow T_A(0.5) = T_B\left(\tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) \Rightarrow T_A = \sqrt{3}T_B\) Resolve vertically: \(T_A\cos 30^\circ + T_B\cos 60^\circ = 24 \Rightarrow T_A\left(\tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) + T_B(0.5)\).

hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(T_A = 12\sqrt{3}\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

question.en: [Practice 3 · Easy] A particle of mass 3 kg is at rest on a smooth horizontal surface. A horizontal force of magnitude P N is applied to the particle, causing it to accelerate at a rate of 4 m/s\(^2\). Find the value of P.

hints.en: According to Newton's Second Law of Motion, the net force acting on an object is equal to the product of its mass and acceleration, i.e., F = ma.

In this case, the mass of the particle is m = 3 kg and its acceleration is a = 4 m/s\(^2\). The applied force P is the net force acting on the particle, as the surface is smooth and horizontal, meaning there are no other horizontal forces to consider.
Thus, the value of P is 12 N.
hints.ar: وعليه، the value of P is 12 N.

solution.en: According to Newton's Second Law of Motion, the net force acting on an object is equal to the product of its mass and acceleration, i.e., F = ma. In this case, the mass of the particle is m = 3 kg and its acceleration is a = 4 m/s\(^2\). The applied force P is the net force acting on the particle, as the surface is smooth and horizontal, meaning there are no other horizontal forces to consider. Therefore, P = ma = (3 kg) * (4 m/s\(^2\)) = 12 N. Thus, the value of P is 12 N.

question.en: [Practice 4 · Medium] A particle of weight \(20\text{ N}\) is suspended in equilibrium by two light inextensible strings inclined at \(30^\circ\) and \(60^\circ\) to the horizontal. Find the exact tensions \(T_1\) and \(T_2\) in the strings.
question.ar: [تدريب 4 · متوسط] جسيم وزنه \(20\text{ N}\) معلّق في حالة اتزان بخيطين خفيفين غير مرنين يميلان بزاويتين \(30^\circ\) و\(60^\circ\) على الأفقي. أوجد قيمتي الشد الدقيقتين \(T_1\) و\(T_2\) في الخيطين.

solution.en:
Resolving horizontally: \(T_1\cos 30^\circ = T_2\cos 60^\circ \implies \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}T_1 = \frac{1}{2}T_2 \implies T_2 = \sqrt{3}\,T_1\).

Resolving vertically: \(\frac{1}{2}T_1 + \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}T_2 = 20\). Substituting \(T_2 = \sqrt{3}\,T_1\) gives \(\frac{1}{2}T_1 + \frac{3}{2}T_1 = 20 \implies 2T_1 = 20\).

Hence \(T_1 = 10\text{ N}\) and \(T_2 = 10\sqrt{3}\text{ N}\).
solution.ar:
بالتحليل الأفقي: \(T_1\cos 30^\circ = T_2\cos 60^\circ \implies T_2 = \sqrt{3}\,T_1\).

بالتحليل الرأسي: \(\frac{1}{2}T_1 + \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}(\sqrt{3}\,T_1) = 20 \implies 2T_1 = 20\).

إذن \(T_1 = 10\text{ N}\) و\(T_2 = 10\sqrt{3}\text{ N}\).

question.en: [Practice 5 · Hard] A parcel of mass \(4\text{ kg}\) rests on a rough plane inclined at \(\theta\) to the horizontal, where \(\sin\theta = \frac{5}{13}\). A force of \(25\text{ N}\) acting parallel and up the plane keeps the parcel on the point of sliding up the plane. Take \(g = 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}\). Find the coefficient of friction \(\mu\) to 3 significant figures.
question.ar: [تدريب 5 · صعب] يستقر طرد كتلته \(4\text{ kg}\) على مستوى خشن يميل بزاوية \(\theta\) على الأفقي حيث \(\sin\theta = \frac{5}{13}\). تؤثر قوة مقدارها \(25\text{ N}\) موازية للمستوى ولأعلى فتجعل الطرد على وشك الانزلاق لأعلى. اعتبر \(g = 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}\). أوجد معامل الاحتكاك \(\mu\) مقرباً إلى 3 أرقام معنوية.

hints.en: Since \(\sin\theta = \frac{5}{13}\), use the \(5\text{-}12\text{-}13\) triangle to write \(\cos\theta = \frac{12}{13}\).
When on the point of moving up the slope, limiting friction acts down the slope: \(25 = mg\sin\theta + F_{\max}\).
hints.ar: عندما يكون الطرد على وشك الحركة لأعلى فإن الاحتكاك الحدّي يعمل لأسفل المستوى: \(25 = mg\sin\theta + F_{\max}\).

solution.en:
From \(\sin\theta = \frac{5}{13}\), we have \(\cos\theta = \frac{12}{13}\). Normal reaction: \(R = 4(9.8)\left(\frac{12}{13}\right) = \frac{470.4}{13}\text{ N}\).

Weight component down the plane: \(mg\sin\theta = 4(9.8)\left(\frac{5}{13}\right) = \frac{196}{13} \approx 15.077\text{ N}\).

Friction acts down the plane at limiting equilibrium: \(F = 25 - \frac{196}{13} = \frac{129}{13}\text{ N}\), so \(\mu = \frac{F}{R} = \frac{129}{470.4} \approx 0.274\) (3 s.f.).
solution.ar:
من \(\sin\theta = \frac{5}{13}\) نجد \(\cos\theta = \frac{12}{13}\). ردّ الفعل العمودي: \(R = 4(9.8)\left(\frac{12}{13}\right) = \frac{470.4}{13}\text{ N}\).

مركّبة الوزن لأسفل المستوى: \(mg\sin\theta = \frac{196}{13}\text{ N}\). ولأن الجسم على وشك الصعود فإن الاحتكاك يعمل لأسفل: \(F = 25 - \frac{196}{13} = \frac{129}{13}\text{ N}\).

إذن معامل الاحتكاك \(\mu = \frac{129}{470.4} \approx 0.274\) (لثلاثة أرقام معنوية).
